claims.text: DistillLens (Dhakal et al., 2026) introduces symmetric knowledge distillation through the Logit Lens, projecting intermediate hidden states into vocabulary space and enforcing structural alignment between student and teacher.
Decoder-based Sense Knowledge Distillation (Wang et al., 2026) addresses a different aspect of intermediate knowledge: structured lexical semantics.

Generative Adversarial Distillation (GAD) (Ye et al., 2025) frames black-box distillation as a minimax game: the student acts as generator while a discriminator learns to distinguish student from teacher responses.
Bounded Behavioral Indistinguishability (Hasan, 2026) challenges the assumption that output similarity implies behavioral equivalence.
PLaD (Zhang et al., 2024) generates pseudo-preference pairs by exploiting teacher-student capacity discrepancies, then uses ranking loss to recalibrate the student's sequence likelihood estimation.
ORPO-Distill (Singh et al., 2025) formulates cross-architecture distillation as preference optimization rather than standard chain-of-thought imitation.
DistiLLM-2 (Ko et al., 2025) introduces a contrastive approach that simultaneously increases the likelihood of teacher responses while decreasing the likelihood of student responses.

Decoupling KL and Trajectories (Zhao et al., 2026) provides a unified theoretical framework showing that off-policy and on-policy distillation implicitly couple two orthogonal choices: prefix source and token-level KL direction.
Knowledge Distillation with Chain-of-Thought RL (Paredes La Torre et al., 2026) combines KD with guided chain-of-thought reinforcement learning using Group Relative Policy Optimization.
Bangladesh Legal RAG (Kamal et al., 2026) addresses legal information accessibility in resource-constrained settings.
Few-Shot MCQA (Sutanto et al., 2024) uses LLMs to generate multiple-choice questions with probability scores, then distills this knowledge into DeBERTa-v3-base.
Parameter reduction: DistillLens achieves improvements without explicit size reduction, focusing on quality gains (Dhakal et al., 2026)
4-bit quantization further reduces memory footprint and latency (Paredes La Torre et al., 2026)
1.6 GB model size enables smartphone deployment (Kamal et al., 2026)
4-8 tokens/second on Pixel 6 without network access (Kamal et al., 2026)
3× reduction in response length via entropy-gated curriculum (Zhao et al., 2026)
Task diversity: Many methods evaluated primarily on instruction-following or math reasoning, with limited cross-domain validation (Dhakal et al., 2026; Zhao et al., 2026)
Adversarial robustness: Behavioral indistinguishability studies reveal that semantic similarity does not guarantee robustness to adversarial probing (Hasan, 2026)

Training complexity: Methods like GAD (Ye et al., 2025) and contrastive approaches (Ko et al., 2025) introduce additional training components (discriminators, dual losses) that increase computational costs
Hyperparameter tuning: Several papers note that optimal settings were determined for specific languages or tasks, requiring re-tuning for new domains (Paredes La Torre et al., 2026)
Loss landscape: While Zhao et al. (2026) provide a unified framework connecting KD objectives to RL paradigms, the interaction between different loss components remains incompletely understood

Information bottlenecks: The mechanisms by which intermediate representations transfer knowledge—and which aspects are most critical—require further investigation (Dhakal et al., 2026; Wang et al., 2026)

Cross-lingual transfer: While Paredes La Torre et al. (2026) and Kamal et al. (2026) demonstrate multilingual capabilities, systematic understanding of language-specific distillation challenges is limited
Unified evaluation frameworks: Standardized adversarial probing suites and behavioral benchmarks (as proposed by Hasan, 2026) should be adopted across distillation research to enable fair comparison
Architecture-agnostic methods: Cross-architecture distillation techniques (Singh et al., 2025; Ko et al., 2025) should be extended to support arbitrary teacher-student pairs without manual alignment
Theoretical foundations: Further work is needed to understand the information-theoretic limits of distillation and the relationship between different loss objectives (Zhao et al., 2026)
